items.title: Section: A New Topic Opens — Deciding the Three Stages of Examination and Reflection

items.zh: 如是已說五識身相應地、意地決擇。有尋有伺等三地決擇，我今當說。
items.en: Thus the deciding discernment of the stage associated with the five sense-consciousness-bodies and the stage of mind has been explained. The deciding discernment of the stages of examination and reflection shall now be explained.

items.title: Section: Not a Tormentor But a Teacher — Why King Yama Deserves the Name "Dharma King"

items.zh: 問：何故焰摩名為法王？為能損害諸眾生故？為能饒益諸眾生故？若由損害眾生，名為法王，不應道理。若由饒益眾生，今應當說云何饒益？答：由能饒益，不由損害。何以故？若諸眾生執到王所，令憶念故，遂為現彼相似之身。告言：汝等自所作業，當受其果。由是因緣，彼諸眾生各自了知，自所作業，還自受果。便於焰摩使者，眾生業力增上所生，猶如變化，非眾生所，無反害心、無瞋恚心，不懷怨恨。乃由此故，感那落迦新業更不積集，故業盡已，脫那落迦趣。是故焰摩由能饒益諸眾生故，名為法王。
items.en: Question: why is Yama called the Dharma King — because he harms beings, or because he benefits them? If because he harms them, this title makes no sense; if because he benefits them, how does he benefit them? Answer: through benefit, not through harm. Why? When beings are dragged before him, in order to help them remember, he causes an image resembling the being they harmed to appear, telling them: you are receiving the fruit of what you yourselves have done. Through this cause, such beings each come to understand that they are receiving the fruit of their own actions, and towards Yama's attendants — a manifestation produced by the increasing force of beings' own karma, like a magical transformation, not truly sentient beings — they give rise to no thought of retaliation, no hatred, and no lingering resentment. Precisely because of this, they cease accumulating any new karma capable of drawing further hellish rebirth, and once their existing karma is exhausted, they are released from the hell realms. It is therefore because he benefits beings that Yama is called the Dharma King.

items.zh: 若諸眾生，生那落迦憶宿命者，焰摩法王更不教誨。若有生已不憶宿命，王便教誨。

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Forgetting, and Why the Ocean Tastes of Salt

items.zh: 略有三種補特伽羅，生那落迦不憶宿命。一、極愚癡。謂生邊地，不解觀察，隨諸惡轉。二、極放逸。謂受欲者，於諸欲中增上耽著，不解觀察，隨諸惡轉。三、極邪見。謂成就一切誹謗邪見，不解觀察，隨諸惡轉。由彼不能自然憶念，故令憶念。復次，二因緣故，大海水鹹。一、生彼眾生福增上故；二、陸地眾生一分非福增上故。所以者何？由水鹹故，非人所涉，生彼無量微細眾生不被採害。又大海中，種種珍寶差別可得，由水鹹故，陸地眾生一分難得。
items.en: There are, in brief, three kinds of beings who, born in the hells, do not remember their past lives. First, extreme ignorance — born in a borderland, unable to reflect and investigate, following wrongdoing. Second, extreme indulgence — one given to sensory pleasure, powerfully absorbed in craving, unable to reflect and investigate, following wrongdoing. Third, extreme wrong view — one who has adopted comprehensive views denying cause and effect, unable to reflect and investigate, following wrongdoing. Since they cannot naturally remember, he causes them to remember. Next, for two reasons the ocean's water is salty: first, because of the increasing merit of beings born there; second, because of a portion of demerit belonging to land-dwelling beings. Why? Because the water's saltiness keeps it from being waded through by humans, so the countless minute beings born there are not caught and killed. Also, the ocean contains all manner of distinct treasures, yet because the water is salty, a portion of land-dwelling beings find them difficult to obtain.

items.title: Section: Sharp Fetters, Dull Fetters — Opening the Vast Study of Affliction

items.zh: 復次，煩惱雜染決擇，我今當說。如先所說煩惱雜染義當知。此煩惱由五種相建立差別。何等為五？一、自性故；二、自性差別故；三、染淨差別故；四、迷斷差別故；五、對治差別故。云何自性？略有二種。一、見性煩惱，二、非見性煩惱。
items.en: Next, the deciding discernment of the defilement of affliction shall now be explained. Its meaning should be understood as already explained earlier. This affliction is established through five distinguishing aspects. What are the five? First, intrinsic nature; second, its specific varieties; third, the distinction between defiled and pure; fourth, the distinction between confusion and severance; fifth, the distinction among antidotes. What is its intrinsic nature? In brief, two kinds: view-natured affliction, and non-view-natured affliction.

items.title: Section: Ten Root Afflictions, Starting with the Self-View Even Animals Are Born With

items.zh: 略有十種。見性煩惱五種差別，非見性者亦有五種，總此十種，名為煩惱自性差別。見性五者，謂薩迦耶見、邊執見、邪見、見取、戒禁取。非見性五者，謂貪、恚、慢、無明、疑。薩迦耶見者，於五取蘊，心執增益，見我、我所，名薩迦耶見。此復二種。一者、俱生，二、分別起。俱生者，一切愚夫異生乃至禽獸並皆現行。分別起者，諸外道等計度而起。
items.en: There are, in brief, ten kinds: five view-natured afflictions, and five non-view-natured. Together these ten are called affliction's own specific varieties. The five view-natured are self-view, extreme view, wrong view, view-attachment, and attachment to wrong precepts and observances. The five non-view-natured are greed, hatred, conceit, ignorance, and doubt. Self-view is clinging, through the mind's superimposing activity, to the five aggregates of clinging, seeing them as self or as belonging to self — this is called self-view. It is further of two kinds: innate, and intellectually adopted. The innate kind manifests in every foolish, ordinary being, down to animals and birds. The intellectually adopted kind arises through various non-Buddhist philosophers' own deliberate reasoning.

items.title: Section: Sixty-Two Wrong Views, Seven Ways to Believe the Self Simply Vanishes

items.zh: 邊執見者，於五取蘊，薩迦耶見增上力故，心執增益，見我斷常，名邊執見。常見所攝邊執見者，謂六十二諸見趣中，計度前際諸遍常論、一分常論，及計後際諸有想論、無想論、非想非非想論。斷見所攝邊執見者，謂諸沙門、若婆羅門七事斷論。此邊執見唯分別起，無有俱生。唯除即此先世已來，串習隨逐邊執見等。若有分別、若無分別差別之相，如本地分已廣分別。邪見者，一切倒見，於所知事顛倒而轉，皆名邪見。
items.en: Extreme view is clinging, through self-view's own increasing power, to the belief that the self is either permanent or annihilated — this is extreme view. Extreme view subsumed under the permanence view refers to, among the sixty-two views, speculation about the past through theories of universal or partial eternity, and speculation about the future through theories of having perception, lacking perception, or neither. Extreme view subsumed under the annihilation view refers to seven theories of annihilation held by various ascetics and brahmins. This extreme view is only ever intellectually adopted, never innate — except where it has, from a former life onward, been so habitually cultivated that it now recurs innately. Wrong view is every distorted understanding, turning away from the true nature of whatever is known — all such views are called wrong view.

blocks.text: Fascicle 58 ascertains the stages "with examination and reflection" (the third to fifth of the seventeen). It soon turns into the treatise's fullest study of affliction.
With examination and reflection; without examination but with reflection; with neither. Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is the "intermediate absorption".

Yama is so called "through benefit, not harm". Master Cháng Bǎi: Yama benefits beings in hell. Those who understand that the hell attendants arise from beings' own karma, like magical transformations, see that he is not a tormentor.

Extreme ignorance, extreme indulgence, extreme wrong view. Master Cháng Bǎi: a "borderland" is a place without the Buddhist fourfold assembly. On why the sea is salty: its many tiny creatures go unharmed by humans; that is their shared karma.

Nature, varieties, establishment, defilement, and antidote; these organise the whole fascicle. Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction is "view-natured" (keen, arising from confusion about principle) or "non-view-natured" (dull, like greed or anger).
Master Cháng Bǎi: innate self-clinging is present from birth, even in animals; the other kind arises from later speculation by those who have not learned the contemplation of no-self.
Master Cháng Bǎi: from habit in former lives, beings have an innate view of permanence or annihilation.
Yama as a teacher, not a torturer: the treatise reverses a familiar fear. Hell itself is made of karma; even its "judge" is a benefactor.

quiz.q: Why is Yama called the Dharma King?
options: through harm: he punishes evildoers with torment and so upholds the law, and beings in the hells, fearing his might, honour him with the title Dharma King
through benefit, not harm: he makes beings remember, so that no new karma accumulates
by keeping the record of life and death and fixing each being's lifespan
by having attained a noble fruit and teaching the Dharma in the hells
quiz.why: The treatise answers that Yama is so called through benefit, not harm. Master Cháng Bǎi: because Yama can benefit beings in hell and does not harm them, he is called the Dharma King. The benefit lies in reminding them, so that they cease to add new karma leading to the hells.

quiz.q: Why do hell-beings feel no wish to retaliate against Yama's attendants, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the attendants are so strong that resistance is useless, and they bide their time
the attendants are emanations of bodhisattvas
they know the attendants arise from karmic force, like magical creations, and are not real beings
hell-beings no longer have any hatred at all
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they understand that the attendants arise through the increasing force of beings' karma, like magical transformations, not real beings; since no new karma is accumulated, when the old is exhausted they leave hell. The English renders this passage accurately.

quiz.q: Which three kinds of beings born in hell do not remember past lives?
options: extreme greed, hatred, and delusion, those heaviest in the three poisons making the deepest karma, the three roots being the basis of the division
those who kill, steal, or commit sexual misconduct
those lacking faculties, eunuchs, and hermaphrodites
extreme ignorance, extreme indulgence, and extreme wrong view
quiz.why: The treatise names extreme ignorance, extreme indulgence, and extreme wrong view. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the borderland as a place without the Buddhist fourfold assembly, where people do not understand cause and effect. Since these cannot naturally recall past lives, Yama helps them remember.

quiz.q: What are the two reasons the ocean's water is salty?
options: rivers carry salt in over long ages
dragon kings spit venom; gods withhold ambrosia
land-dwellers' merit; sea creatures' demerit
the increasing merit of beings born there; a portion of land-dwellers' demerit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the many tiny creatures of the sea are not killed by humans, which is their shared karma and merit. Land-dwellers, for their part, find the sea's treasures hard to obtain. So the salt has a karmic reading both ways.

quiz.q: The English has "the stages of examination and reflection." What is the problem?
options: no problem: these are just the examination and reflection stages, fully covered by the English, and the lecture treats only one stage
the problem is "examination," which should be "test"
the problem is "stages," which should be "realms"
it drops 等三地: the stages without examination are lost, and all seem to have both
quiz.why: The three stages are with examination and reflection, without examination but with reflection, and with neither. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the second as the intermediate absorption, and the third as the second absorption upwards with the formless heavens. "The stages of examination and reflection" loses the two latter stages.

quiz.q: Through which five aspects is the defilement of affliction distinguished?
options: the three realms, the path of vision, and the path of cultivation
greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, and doubt
manifestation, latent tendency, heaviness, residue, and outflow
nature, varieties, defiled and pure, confusion and severance, and antidotes
quiz.why: These five organise the whole discussion of this fascicle. Master Cháng Bǎi: intrinsic nature is the two kinds, view-natured and non-view-natured; the varieties are the ten root and the secondary afflictions; confusion and severance concern delusion about the four truths and the two severings.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi separate view-natured and non-view-natured afflictions?
options: the view-natured belong only to outsiders and the other to all, the difference lying in whether one has studied the Dharma, not in whether principle or matter is confused
view-natured is wholesome; the other unwholesome
view-natured confuses the truths' principle, keenly; non-view-natured mostly clings to worldly things
view-natured arises with eye-consciousness; the other with mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: view-natured afflictions arise in thought through confusion about the four truths' principle, wrong knowledge and ideas, and are the keen kind; non-view-natured ones, such as greed, hatred, conceit, and ignorance, arise mainly from clinging to worldly things.

quiz.q: How do innate and intellectually adopted self-view differ?
options: innate: only outsiders; adopted: all ordinary beings and animals
innate: all ordinary beings down to animals manifest it; adopted: outsiders arrive at it by speculation
innate belongs to the higher realms; adopted to the desire realm
innate is severed by vision; adopted by cultivation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: innate self-clinging is present from birth; the other arises from later discrimination, when those outside the Dharma, not having learned the contemplation of no-self, speculate in thought. So even animals have the innate kind. The English "intellectually adopted" is a clear rendering.

quiz.q: The English has "recurs as though innate." Is "as though" fitting?
options: yes: extreme view is never innate, the prior clause admitting no exception, so habit can only resemble the innate, as "as though" exactly says
no: it should read "as though annihilated"
no: the Chinese speaks of the next life
no: the lecture says innate views really exist in this life; "as though" is an addition that weakens this
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from former lives, by constant habituation, there is in this life naturally an innate view of permanence or annihilation. 唯除 marks a real exception. The English "as though innate" adds a hedge the Chinese does not have, and treats the exception as only apparent.
